children: Gold gains 0.4% early in Asian trade but remains at more than one-year lows as markets price in rate increases from the Fed. The precious metal has been under pressure from a strong dollar and expectations that the Fed will tilt more hawkish to rein in inflation. Minutes from the Fed's October meeting cemented those views, showing that nearly all members thought tighter policy will ultimately be needed under their most likely scenario for the economy. A few warned that inflation might prove stickier than expected, which could necessitate a shift to a more restrictive stance. Chart-wise, it's difficult to spot any significant level of support until prices hit $3,500 an ounce, says David Morrison at Trade Nation. Gold last at $3,739 an ounce. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
